intro.label: Intimate
intro.use: Close friends, younger siblings and cousins; an elder to a child, with love. From a stranger it is rude.

intro.label: Familiar
intro.use: Friends, family (often parents too) and children. Also people your age once you know them.

intro.label: Respectful
intro.use: Elders, strangers, teachers, shopkeepers, drivers, and anyone at work. When in doubt, use this.

tiers.title: Who is this?
tiers.description: Pick তুই, তুমি or আপনি for the person in front of you.

tiers.title: Match the verb
tiers.description: Pick the verb ending that goes with the pronoun: present, future and commands.

tiers.title: Say it right
tiers.description: Pick the whole sentence that fits the person and the situation.

tiers.title: Tricky cases
tiers.description: Families, affection, rudeness and work: where the simple rules bend.

scenarios.situation: You visit your grandmother (your father's mother, your দাদি). Which "you" do you use with her?
scenarios.why: Grandparents are elders, so আপনি is the safe, respectful choice. Many families use তুমি with grandparents as a sign of closeness. তুই upward sounds rude.
scenarios.varies: Both are heard: আপনি is never wrong with a grandparent; many families use তুমি with their grandmother.

scenarios.situation: You stop a rickshaw on a Dhaka street. The driver is older than you.
scenarios.why: An adult stranger gets আপনি. People often call a rickshaw driver মামা or ভাই, but the pronoun should still be আপনি; তুমি or তুই to a worker talks down to him.

scenarios.situation: You are buying vegetables from a middle-aged shopkeeper at the bazaar.
scenarios.why: A shopkeeper is an adult you don't know well: আপনি. You can still call him ভাই (or a woman আপা) to sound friendly.

scenarios.situation: Your eight-year-old cousin wants to play with you.
scenarios.why: Children and younger relatives get তুমি. Within the family, তুই to a younger cousin is common and sounds warm, not rude.
scenarios.varies: Both are heard: তুমি is gentle and always fine; many families use তুই with younger cousins and siblings.

scenarios.situation: You are chatting with your best friend from school. You are the same age and have known each other for years.
scenarios.why: Close friends of the same age usually use তুই with each other: it is the most intimate "you". Friends who are less close stay with তুমি.

scenarios.situation: You ask your teacher a question after class.
scenarios.why: Teachers always get আপনি, however friendly they are.

scenarios.situation: A neighbour's five-year-old child waves at you.
scenarios.why: Small children get তুমি from adults they don't live with. আপনি to a child sounds odd, and তুই from a near stranger can sound rough.

scenarios.situation: At a bus stop you ask a stranger about your own age which bus goes to the station.
scenarios.why: Adult strangers get আপনি, even if they are your age. You move to তুমি only once you know each other.

scenarios.situation: You greet your boss at the office in the morning.
scenarios.why: At work, a boss gets আপনি. Many Bangladeshi offices use আপনি in both directions.

scenarios.situation: You find your two closest friends waiting for you. You want to ask where they all are going. Which plural "you"?
scenarios.why: The plurals follow the same scale: তোরা (intimate), তোমরা (familiar), আপনারা (polite). Close friends you call তুই become তোরা together.

scenarios.situation: Your parents' elderly friends arrive as guests. You speak to all of them together.
scenarios.why: A group of elders gets আপনারা, the plural of আপনি.

scenarios.situation: You meet a cousin your age whom you call তুমি. Fill in the verb.
scenarios.why: তুমি takes the familiar ending -ো: তুমি আছো. আছিস goes with তুই and আছেন with আপনি.
scenarios.notes: Kolkata spelling often leaves off the final vowel sign of আছো; the word is the same.

scenarios.situation: You greet your friend's father. Fill in the verb.
scenarios.why: আপনি always takes the polite ending -েন: আছেন, খান, করেন.

scenarios.situation: You offer tea to an older neighbour. Fill in the verb.
scenarios.why: With আপনি the verb ends in -ন or -েন: চান. চাও is the তুমি form and চাস the তুই form.

scenarios.situation: You ask your younger brother, whom you call তুই, a question. Fill in the verb.
scenarios.why: তুই takes the intimate ending -স or -িস: খাস, করিস, আছিস.

scenarios.situation: You ask a new friend your age, whom you call তুমি, about their job. Fill in the verb.
scenarios.why: তুমি + present = the -ো form: করো. The same form is also the তুমি command ("do!").

scenarios.situation: A visitor in a shop asks you a question. They use আপনি with you, and you use আপনি back. Fill in the verb.
scenarios.why: "Can" follows the same pattern: পারিস (তুই), পারো (তুমি), পারেন (আপনি).

scenarios.situation: You ask your mother for water. You call her তুমি. Pick the command.
scenarios.why: The তুমি command is the same as the তুমি present: দাও. দে is the তুই command; দিন is for আপনি.

scenarios.situation: You ask your best friend, whom you call তুই, for water. Pick the command.
scenarios.why: The তুই command is the bare stem: দে. Between close friends it sounds friendly, not bossy.

scenarios.situation: An elderly uncle comes to visit. You invite him to sit. Pick the command.
scenarios.why: আপনি has two commands: everyday Bangladeshi বসেন (the আপনি present) and standard বসুন (-উন). বসো is for তুমি.
scenarios.varies: Both are heard: বসেন is everyday Bangladeshi speech; বসুন is the standard form, used in formal settings and in Kolkata.
scenarios.notes: In Kolkata বসুন is the usual polite command; বসেন sounds Bangladeshi.

scenarios.situation: You call a small child over to you. Pick the command.
scenarios.why: A child gets তুমি, so the familiar command এসো. আসুন and আসবেন are polite invitations for adults.

scenarios.situation: You ask a rickshaw driver (you call him মামা) if he will go to Dhanmondi. Pick the verb.
scenarios.why: Calling a rickshaw driver মামা is friendly, but the verb stays polite: যাবেন. যাবি or যাবে would talk down to him.

scenarios.situation: You visit your grandmother (your mother's mother, your নানি) at lunchtime. Ask if she has eaten.
scenarios.why: The pronoun and verb must match: আপনি … খেয়েছেন, তুমি … খেয়েছো. আপনি with the তুমি ending খেয়েছো is a mistake.
scenarios.varies: Both are heard: আপনি is respectful; many families say তুমি to a grandmother. Just keep the verb matching the pronoun.

scenarios.situation: At the bazaar, ask the shopkeeper (you call him ভাই) for two kilos of potatoes.

options.bn: ভাই, আমাকে দুই কেজি আলু দেন।
options.tr: bhai, amake dui keji alu den
options.en: Brother, give me two kilos of potatoes.

options.bn: ভাই, আমাকে দুই কেজি আলু দে।
options.tr: bhai, amake dui keji alu de
options.en: Brother, give me two kilos of potatoes. (intimate)

options.bn: ভাই, আমাকে দুই কেজি আলু দাও।
options.tr: bhai, amake dui keji alu dao
options.en: Brother, give me two kilos of potatoes. (familiar)

scenarios.why: A shopkeeper gets the polite command দেন (or standard দিন). ভাই is friendly, but it does not make তুই or তুমি polite.

scenarios.situation: Invite your best friend, whom you call তুই, to come tomorrow.
scenarios.why: তুই takes the -ি future: আসবি. আপনি to your best friend would sound cold, and তুই with আসবেন mixes two levels.

scenarios.situation: Ask your boss if she can help you.

options.bn: আপনি কি আমাকে সাহায্য করতে পারবেন?
options.tr: apni ki amake shahajjo korte parben?

options.bn: তুমি কি আমাকে সাহায্য করতে পারবে?
options.tr: tumi ki amake shahajjo korte parbe?

options.bn: আপনি কি আমাকে সাহায্য করতে পারবে?
options.tr: apni ki amake shahajjo korte parbe?

scenarios.why: A boss gets আপনি with the polite future পারবেন. পারবে is the তুমি form, so it doesn't go with আপনি.

scenarios.situation: Ask a little girl you have just met what her name is.
scenarios.why: "Your" changes with the pronoun too: তোর (তুই), তোমার (তুমি), আপনার (আপনি). A child gets তোমার; তোর from a stranger sounds rough.

scenarios.situation: On a train, ask a stranger your age where they have come from.

options.en: Where have I come from? (wrong person)

scenarios.why: A stranger gets আপনি, and আপনি takes -েন: এসেছেন. এসেছি is the "I" form.

scenarios.situation: Your teacher is speaking too fast. Ask her to speak a little more slowly.

options.en: Please speak a little slowly. (everyday polite)

scenarios.why: A teacher gets an আপনি command: standard বলুন or everyday বলেন. বলো is the তুমি command.
scenarios.varies: Both are heard: বলুন is standard and very polite; বলেন is the everyday Bangladeshi polite command.
scenarios.notes: In Kolkata বলুন is the norm; বলেন as a command sounds Bangladeshi.

scenarios.situation: Your younger sister is nervous before an exam. Tell her not to worry.
scenarios.why: A younger sibling gets তুই or তুমি, so করিস না or করো না. করবেন না is the polite "don't", for elders and strangers.
scenarios.varies: Both are heard: some families use তুই between siblings, others তুমি.

scenarios.situation: Your friend's mother (you call her আন্টি) is at your door. Invite her in.
scenarios.why: An adult guest gets the polite command আসুন. এসো is how you'd call a child, and আসবি is for close friends only.

scenarios.situation: You are with a group of close friends and want to leave. Say "Let's go."
scenarios.why: "Let's" has three levels too: চল (তুই), চলো (তুমি), চলেন (আপনি). Close friends use চল or চলো.
scenarios.varies: Both are heard: friends who use তুই say চল; friends who use তুমি say চলো.

scenarios.situation: You are talking to your father (আব্বু). Which "you" do Bangladeshi families use?
scenarios.why: Most urban families today use তুমি with both parents. In many older or rural families children say আপনি to their father, and sometimes to both parents. তুই to a parent is never polite.
scenarios.varies: Both are heard: তুমি is the most common today; some families use আপনি, especially with fathers. Follow your own family's habit.

scenarios.situation: Your grandfather (দাদা) always calls you তুই, with love. You answer him. Which "you" do you use back?
scenarios.why: An elder's তুই is affectionate, but it is not returned. You answer with তুমি or আপনি, as your family does.
scenarios.varies: Both are heard: some families use তুমি with grandparents, others আপনি.
scenarios.notes: In Kolkata দাদা means elder brother; a father's father has a different name there.

scenarios.situation: In a restaurant, the man at the next table calls the young waiter তুই. You want to ask the waiter for water. Which "you" do you use?
scenarios.why: তুই from a stranger, especially to someone serving you, is talking down. তুমি to young service staff is very common but still a little condescending. আপনি is the respectful choice.

scenarios.situation: You are 30. A teenager you don't know, about 16, asks you for directions.
scenarios.why: With a younger stranger both are possible: তুমি to a teenager is normal, and আপনি is polite and never wrong. Avoid তুই with someone you don't know.
scenarios.varies: Both are heard: many adults use তুমি with teenagers; others use আপনি with any stranger.

scenarios.situation: You call your best friend তুই. Now you greet your best friend's mother.
scenarios.why: Each person gets their own level: your friend is তুই, but your friend's mother is an elder, so আপনি. If you grew up in her house you may use তুমি with her.

scenarios.situation: A colleague your age, whom you've been calling আপনি, says: "আমাকে তুমি বলো।" ("Call me তুমি.") Ask how they are.
scenarios.why: People move from আপনি to তুমি when they become friends, often with exactly this request. তুই is a further step that only close friends take.

scenarios.situation: Only one of these sentences is correct Bengali. Which one?
scenarios.why: আপনি goes with চান and তুমি with চাও. Mixing a pronoun with another level's ending is the most common learner mistake.

scenarios.situation: You tell a friend about your teacher, who is not there. Formality applies to "he/she" too.
scenarios.why: Someone you would call আপনি is উনি when you talk about them (তিনি in writing). ও and সে are for friends, children and people you'd call তুমি or তুই.

scenarios.situation: Your close friends are sitting with their parents. You ask the whole group how they are.
scenarios.why: With a mixed group, use the level of its most senior members: আপনারা. তোরা would include the parents in your intimate তুই.

scenarios.situation: Your new manager is five years younger than you. Ask if she is coming to the office today.

options.en: Are you coming to the office today?
Are you coming to the office today? (familiar)
Are you coming to the office today? (intimate)

scenarios.why: Age is not the only thing that counts: at work, role and distance matter too. A manager gets আপনি, whatever her age.
